title: B-Roll Shot List
subtitle: One consolidated list. Duplicates merged. Shot names you can call on set.
howToUse: Pick 8–12 shots per film, not the whole menu. Prefer real Dopami UI, real teammates, and real rooms. Crop every screen so Slack, WhatsApp, dashboards, and documents are unreadable. Never film handheld while driving.

categories.title: Deep work & focus
categories.blurb: Use these to show you entering flow — the visual language of building, not posing.

shots.frame: Camera behind you. Laptop or bag in hand as you enter and sit.
shots.why: Establishing beat. Opens a day-in-the-life sequence.

shots.frame: Close-up of hands opening the lid; screen lights up.
Side profile, tight on ear. Slip on over-ears; cut ambient sound on the snap.
shots.why: Universal shorthand for “flow state starts now.”

shots.frame: 60fps tight shot, shallow DOF. Fingers on keys; rack focus keycaps → wrist.
shots.why: Tactile motion that carries sound design.

shots.frame: 45° behind the hand. Fast two-finger scroll through a board, backlog, or Figma canvas.
shots.why: Shows scale and volume in half a second.

shots.frame: Extreme close-up of eye or glasses in a dim room. Screen colors shift across the surface.
shots.why: Signals intense analysis without leaking private data.

shots.frame: Low floor angle looking up. Sit-to-stand desk lifts as you step into frame.
shots.why: Vertical movement that breaks talking-head fatigue.

shots.frame: Top-down. Flip a sand timer or tap start on a watch / focus app.
shots.why: Puts stakes on the next scene.

shots.frame: Inside looking out. Door pulled shut; latch clicks.
Overhead flat lay. Uncap a pen and cross off a finished line.
shots.why: Satisfying closure; viewers pause to read.

shots.frame: Slow track from behind the chair. Head turns between reference and live work.
shots.why: Makes desktop work feel spatial, not static.

shots.frame: Medium shot across the desk. Lean back, rub temple, exhale, dive back in.
shots.why: Humanizes the grind between typing shots.

categories.title: Product & design craft
categories.blurb: Proof you are actually building. Prefer the real Dopami UI over generic mockups.

shots.frame: Macro on screen. Cursor drags a card or frame into perfect alignment.
shots.why: Craft and precision. Speaks to designers.

shots.frame: Top-down 45°, phone on desk. Thumb runs through real screen transitions.
Testing Dopami on your phone while walking.
Edit something, then watch the live UI update.
shots.why: Shows iteration, not a finished demo.

shots.frame: Pan across phone, tablet, laptop. Tap mobile; laptop state updates.
Hold a rough paper sketch next to the finished screen, or cut paper → wireframe → UI.
Over-shoulder on iPad. Boxes, circles, layout lines.
60fps or time-lapse following a marker tip: journeys, arrows, architecture.
Peel a note from Backlog and slap it onto Shipped.
Record a product thought into the phone.
You facing a large screen of growth / retention charts. No private numbers readable.
Rack focus onto a chart. Finger follows a line up and to the right.
Side angle. Mouse stops, head tilts, you lean 3 inches closer.
Extreme close-up of the index finger on Submit / Deploy / Launch.
High-contrast crop. Hit Enter; build text cascades.
shots.why: Codes you as close to the builders. Use only if true.

categories.title: Thinking, research & the ADHD angle
categories.blurb: Best for “what I believe / future I’m building / lessons” films. On-brand for Dopami.

shots.frame: Alone, no phone performance. Medium or behind.
Looking out; traffic or skyline below.
Laptop open, eyes off the screen.
shots.why: Thinking is not the same as typing.

shots.frame: Write a single line in a notebook and stop.
Pages of earlier notes, diagrams, messy thinking.
shots.why: Continuity of the work over time.

shots.frame: Mark a sentence in a book, paper, or printout.
Finish the thought, close the cover.
Stand still, look, then make the first mark.
Close-up of studies or notes — no copyrighted page filling the frame.
Highlight / scribble on a printed paper.
Timer running; you deep in work. Same family as Deep Work shots.
Done Together / community grid on screen, carefully framed.
shots.why: Shows the actual mechanism, not a slogan.

shots.frame: Sticky notes of real (anonymized) feedback.
shots.why: Users in the room without putting faces on camera.

shots.frame: Stylized notification on phone — dramatized, not a private message.
Split or match-cut: messy desk to reset desk.

categories.title: Team, leadership & war room
categories.blurb: Use real people and real rooms. Crop so Slack, WhatsApp, and dashboards never leak private text.

shots.frame: Office door opens; you enter. Or wide of you arriving.
2–4 people, mid-discussion, not posed at camera.
Leaning in, pointing at a line or chart, reacting together.
Slow push-in on a grid. Speaking indicators moving. No readable chat.
You on a team call; camera behind the laptop.
Hand writing while the call runs off-camera or blurred.
Reverse track ahead of two people debating a product call.
More than one person writing.
Candid coding / building. No shoulder-tap posing.
shots.why: CTO as a real person in the story.

shots.frame: Reviewing a sheet or model, mid-work.
shots.why: Ops / numbers as part of the culture.

shots.frame: One person at the board or deck; others watching.
You spin or tap a marker while listening to an engineer.
Handheld, slightly imperfect, over a desk after a blocker clears.
Profile, window side-light. Chin on hand, processing.
shots.why: Cutaway for failure, pivot, hard calls.

shots.frame: Low side angle. Clicker press; slide changes in the background.
Candid, not a brand campaign smile-hold.
Group walking mid-conversation.

categories.title: Daily routine, fitness & founder life
categories.blurb: Lifestyle glue. Shoot once, reuse for months. Keep gym and commute honest — no costume discipline.

shots.frame: Silhouette. Blinds open; early light washes the room.
Macro, 60–120fps. Extraction, steam, pour. Or a simple kitchen make.
Close-up of fastening a watch.
Floor-level. Tie, heel tap, stand out of frame.
Hands collecting the kit on the way out.
Ground-level rear. Pack up, one-shoulder sling, walk out.
Low side track, level with the deck. Steady cadence.
Sleeve clang, or hands wrapping knurled steel with chalk puff.
shots.why: Grit. Only if this is actually your training.

shots.frame: Wide, backlit. Hands on knees or towel, chest working.
shots.why: Unpolished counterweight to shiny product shots.

shots.frame: Top-down. Chop, crack eggs, assemble.
shots.why: Habits as operations, not influencer meal-prep.

shots.frame: Bag, charger, notebook going in.

categories.title: Human & emotional beats
categories.blurb: These stop the film from looking like LinkedIn cosplay. Short. Unperformed. One or two per piece.

shots.frame: Tiny exhale after something works.
Something shipped or a message landed. Keep it small.
shots.why: Earns more than a staged laugh.

shots.frame: Look at the phone, then a real reaction.
Frustration, then stop.
shots.why: The day is not only flow state.

shots.frame: Reset after the above.
Sit. Don’t act tired — just stop performing.
The two seconds after a take when posture drops.
shots.why: Humility. Best podcast B-roll you can steal.

shots.frame: Umbrella optional. Don’t romanticize it into a perfume ad.
Same family as thinking walks, warmer light.
You looking at the city, not the camera.
You leave frame into a large environment.

categories.title: Media, podcast & community
categories.blurb: For talking-head, interview, and “I record this so you don’t have to” content.

shots.frame: Wide. Articulated boom swings to your mouth.
shots.why: Signals an insight or interview is coming.

shots.frame: First person, looking down at the rig. Cap twists off; room snaps sharp.
60fps, centered. One sharp clap in front of the lens.
shots.why: Audio-visual hook in the first 2 seconds.

shots.frame: ECU of eyes tracking bullets, then into the lens.
Screen crop. Scrub dense vocals, snap a split.
shots.why: Shows deliberate editing. Speaks to creators.

shots.frame: Wide corner, 8–16x. Lights up, tripod, cables, empty room filling.
Walking, gesturing, not looking at camera.

categories.title: Transitions, transit & texture
categories.blurb: The connective tissue. Shoot a bank of these once; they cover cuts, location changes, and pacing.

shots.frame: Centered, facing out. Doors open or seal to black.
Low, symmetrical. You stand; camera rises into daylight.
shots.why: Linear motion that holds edit energy.

shots.frame: Busy pavement, Delhi-NCR texture. You moving through, not posing.
shots.why: Place. Don’t stock-replace it with generic downtown.

shots.frame: Get in, or walk away from the car after arriving. Driving only from a mounted / passenger camera — never handheld while driving.
Profile on your reflection; city streaking behind.
Low gimbal past glass buildings, long shadows.
Steaming mug on a high-rise ledge. Rack focus drops → city.
Coffee/chai steam in the same frame as the machine.
Dust in the beam. Slow.
One object, held.
Pages lift.
Reach, lift, or lock.
shots.why: Tiny action that covers a jump cut.

shots.frame: Time as a motif, not a countdown gimmick.
Feet only, commute cadence.

shots.shot: Wide workspace at open of day
shots.frame: Empty or just-started desk. Establishing.
Dark room, one warm lamp. Hand clicks it; room goes blue-black.

filmingOrder: Home / morning first: blinds, coffee, watch, bag, laptop open. Natural light dies quickly.
Desk block next: typing, headphones, timer, notebook, Figma, phone prototype, dashboards. Same shirt, same desk.
Then team: huddles, Ankit, Somalika, whiteboard, chai. People are the scarce resource.
Transit last: elevator, street, window, golden hour, lamp off. These are reusable across many films.
Emotional beats are not a separate setup — grab them inside the desk and walk blocks when they actually happen.
privacyChecklist: Blur or crop every chat, email, customer name, and metric that is not meant to be public.
Ask teammates before any face-forward shot. Candid is not the same as consented.
Don’t put copyrighted paper or a full article page on screen.
Driving shots: passenger seat or a mounted camera only.
tips: Pick 8–12 shots per film, not the whole menu.

Crop every screen so Slack, WhatsApp, dashboards, and documents are unreadable.
Never film handheld while driving — passenger seat or a mounted camera only.
Shoot the keyboard macro at 60fps with a shallow depth of field — tactile motion that carries sound design.
Ask teammates before any face-forward shot. Candid is not the same as consented.
Don't put copyrighted paper or a full article page on screen.
Blur or crop every chat, email, customer name, and metric that isn't meant to be public.
Shoot home and morning scenes first — natural light dies quickly.
Group desk-block shots together: typing, headphones, timer, notebook, Figma, phone prototype — same shirt, same desk.
Save transit shots (elevator, street, window, golden hour, lamp off) for last — they're reusable across many films.
Grab emotional beats inside the desk and walk blocks when they actually happen. Don't stage a separate setup for them.
A small, real smile at the screen earns more than a staged laugh.
Keep gym and commute shots honest — no costume discipline.
One sharp clap in frame at 60fps gives you an audio-visual sync hook in the first two seconds.
Time-lapse the whiteboard flow — it anchors strategy voiceover better than a static hold.
Don't over-stage the fist bump — a slightly imperfect handheld take beats a posed one.
Shoot a bank of transition shots once (elevators, escalators, doors) — they cover cuts and pacing across many future edits.
Rack focus from a chart to a finger tracing the line — the clearest way to show traction without reading numbers.
People are the scarce resource on shoot day — schedule team shots (huddles, whiteboard, chai) in one block.
